questions.question: What color are warning signs for hazardous locations?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black letters.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Pay attention to these signs.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body gets rid of about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your riding ability.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can affect your riding. Impairment starts well below the legal limit.

questions.question: If you lock the rear brake on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a good road, keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How should you cross railroad tracks that are at an angle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight in your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight in your lane when crossing angled tracks. Turning to cross at a right angle can move you into another lane.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing anytime you ride. Crashes happen day and night, so always wear visible clothing.

questions.question: What happens when you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is okay as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is okay as long as no other vehicles are nearby.
You may move into another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may move into another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may end up in another lane or off the road. Always slow down for turns.

questions.question: What does a plastic face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield.

questions.question: How do you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, what is safest?

options.text: One rider passes completely before the next rider begins.
Several riders pass at the same time.
The last rider waves to signal no more motorcycles are coming.
Riders pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One rider passes completely before the next rider begins.
questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must complete their pass and return to position before the next rider passes.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your whole head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance while turning. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should riders do?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Use the horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Ride directly in front of other vehicles so their headlights can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes slowing down, increasing your distance from other vehicles, using the lights of cars ahead to see farther, using your high beam headlight when safe, and changing your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid a slippery road?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to keep your balance.
Keep your speed the same to improve grip.
Do not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid slippery roads completely. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change. Choose a position that gives you the most space and makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders ride when in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This way, more experienced riders at the back can watch them.

questions.question: In New York, how many years does a motorcycle registration last?
questions.correctAnswerText: One year.
questions.explanation: Most vehicle registrations in New York State last two years. But motorcycle registrations only last one year and expire on April 30.

questions.question: Which sign has a rectangular shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means to go carefully. When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, slow down and look for hazards.
